# OI:LOOP

> Weights in Light. Compute in Motion. OI:LOOP prints the weights of large language models into passive optical processors and sells low-cost AI inference tokens from its own facility. It does not sell chips.

## Product
- PMP-1550 Zero-Gate Passive Matrix Processor: model weights printed into glass as optical paths (optical polymer on glass, UV lithography).
- Weight cell: non-resonant passive attenuator; weight = share of light transmitted. No heaters, no clock; the weight bank draws 0 W.
- One pass of 1550 nm light performs every multiplication of a matrix at once; propagation time does not depend on matrix size.
- Optical scope: MLP layers, about 81% of multiplies per token. Electronics handle activations and attention.

## Key figures (design targets and models, not measurements)
- Energy per multiply: 3.3–6.3 fJ in the core design model, 30–60x less than a current flagship GPU (~200 fJ) at core level.
- Accuracy simulation on a half-billion-parameter model: 8-bit weights +0.04 perplexity; 1% optical weight error +0.13.
- Plan: year 2 a half-billion-parameter model end to end; year 3 a ~100B mixture-of-experts pilot; year 4 a 700B-class model; year 5 three 700B-class models.

## Stage
- Architecture, material, energy model and accuracy simulation complete. Nothing fabricated yet. Next: print and measure an 8x8 weight bank, then a 64x64 tile.

## FAQ
- Q: What is OI:LOOP?
  A: OI:LOOP is an early-stage company that prints the weights of large language models into passive optical processors and sells low-cost AI inference tokens from its own facility. It does not sell chips.
- Q: How does a passive optical processor run an AI model?
  A: The input is written onto 1550 nm light. The light passes a glass panel where each printed path transmits a fixed share of light, and that share is the weight. Detectors sum the products. Every multiplication of a matrix happens in one pass of light, and electronics handle activations and attention.
- Q: How much energy can it save?
  A: In OI:LOOP's core-level design model, the passive bank uses 3.3–6.3 femtojoules per multiply, 30–60 times less than a current flagship GPU at about 200 fJ. This is a design model, not yet a measurement.
- Q: Why does the weight bank use no power?
  A: The weights are fixed optical paths, not memory cells. There are no heaters, transistors or clocks in the bank, so it draws 0 W. Power goes to the laser, modulators, detectors and converters.
- Q: Which models will OI:LOOP run?
  A: First a half-billion-parameter language model end to end, then a ~100B-class mixture-of-experts pilot, then 700B-class models. One printed panel set carries one model version.
- Q: What stage is OI:LOOP at?
  A: Architecture, material choice, energy model and accuracy simulation are complete. Nothing has been fabricated yet. The next milestone is printing and measuring an 8×8 weight bank, then a 64×64 tile.
- Q: Why 1550 nm?
  A: 1550 nm is the wavelength of fibre-optic networks, so lasers, fibres, modulators and detectors are mature, low-cost telecom parts.
- Q: How do I get access?
  A: Join the early waitlist on oiloop.com, write to info@oiloop.com, or connect your AI assistant to the OI:LOOP MCP server at https://oiloop.com/mcp.
